24.7.3.en: The Jesuit translation has: "And in the cities men groan," so injustice does not stop at the villages but extends also to the cities.

24.7.4.en: "God does not pay attention to injustice," that is, He does not judge them quickly, but gives them time, that perhaps they may repent, returning to Him. He prolongs His longsuffering toward them, and may leave them all their life on earth, and not expose their folly here, until their souls are required, and they are counted fools and silly. As it was said to the rich man shortly before his soul was required: "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee" (Lk 12:20). And as it was said of the rich man who gathers wealth by injustice: "He that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the midst of his days, and at his end shall be a fool" (Jer 17:11).

24.7.5.en: * [They cause men to groan from out of the cities] [12]. Cities are so called from the people who live together, and so the churches of the true faith are not improperly expressed by the cities... For this harmony among the people who live together was established by the Lord in the Gospels, even when He distinguished between places, when He wished to feed the people with five loaves. He commanded them to sit down by fifties or by hundreds in orderly arrangement, so that the multitudes of the believers might take their food in separate places but united together... But the heretics often shatter the united life and harmony of the good by attaching themselves to those in authority among the wicked of this world; therefore it was rightly said in this place: [they cause men to groan from out of the cities].

24.7.6.en: [The soul of the wounded crieth out]... for the soul of the righteous is wounded when the faith of the weak is shaken... But God does not allow him (the wicked) to pass without punishment.

24.7.8.en: They are among those that rebel against the light.

24.8.0.en: They know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof [13].

24.8.1.en: Since the wicked think that God does not care about His believers, and does not move in the face of the injustice that falls upon them, they rebel against God, the true Light. And they lose insight and are struck with blindness, so they do not know the ways of God, nor walk in His paths.

24.8.2.en: Some see that those who sin against the light of the divine commandment, while confessing that they know God, the true Light, are nevertheless rebels against this knowledge that they have received, for they do not wish to walk according to it.

24.8.3.en: Others interpret this phrase literally. Although they have the light of day, they choose the night that suits their evils; for this reason evils are called "the works of darkness" (Eph 5:11): "For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God" (Jn 3:20-21).

24.8.4.en: * For those who first rebelled while knowing afterward became blind and no longer know, as it is written: [Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful] (Rom 21:1, 28). It is added concerning them a little later: [God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient]. For since they did not wish to glorify Him whom they knew, they were given a sense of rejection, and were left to this fate, that they no longer know how to appreciate the evils that they have done... Now those who do not care to do the plain good works no longer receive understanding of what is purer.

24.8.6.en: * Thus, when the Lord Jesus saw the heavy burdens of the sinner, He wept. For He did not allow the Church alone to weep, but we see Him also having compassion on His beloved, and saying to the dead man, "Come forth" (Jn 11:43). That is, you who were cast into the darkness of conscience and the captivity of your sins and the prison of your crimes, come forth. Show your sins and you will be justified, for "with the mouth confession is made unto salvation" (Rom 10:10)...

24.8.7.en: Grant me, O Lord, that You come to my tomb and pour out tears over me, for my eyes have dried up and are no longer able to pour out such tears for my transgressions. If You weep, O Lord, over me (as over Lazarus), I shall be rescued... You call me from this tomb of my body, saying: "Come forth," so that my thinking may no longer be confined within the limits of this narrow body of mine, but go out toward Christ and live in the light, and I no longer think of the works of darkness but of the works of light.

24.9.0.en: 14 The murderer riseth with the light, he killeth the poor and needy, and in the night he is as a thief. 15 The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the evening, saying, No eye shall watch me: and he putteth a covering on his face. 16 In the dark they dig through houses; in the daytime they shut themselves up. They know not the light. 17 For the morning is to them the same as the shadow of death: for they know the terrors of the shadow of death.

24.9.1.en: The murderer riseth with the light.

24.9.2.en: He killeth the poor and needy, and in the night he is as a thief [14].

24.9.3.en: Job presents to us three kinds of wicked men who flee from the light: the murderer, who even if he kills in the daytime flees from the light like a thief hiding in the midst of the darkness.

24.9.4.en: And the adulterer, who waits for the coming of evening to practice his evil, thinking that the darkness hides his evil from the eyes of men; and the one who digs through houses, who shuts himself up in the daytime and sees that the night makes it easy for him to attack houses and escape.

24.9.5.en: When the wicked man rebels and defies God, and rises against the believers to kill them, he is like the murderer who in boldness kills openly in the midst of the day, aware that there is no one who can stand before him and stop him. He kills the poor and needy, not caring about the Father of the poor. Since he does this in defiance of God, the true Light, the darkness of his wicked deeds comes upon him, and he is like the thief who works in the darkness of the night. He is called a thief working by night after having been a bold murderer killing in the midst of the light of day. For after a man practices his evils with violence, without fear even of God, sin robs him of his strength and courage, and he becomes feeble and fears even his own shadow, so he is like a thief who is afraid lest someone catch him.

24.9.6.en: * "And in the night he is as a thief" [14]. For in the night of his temptations, although without strength, he shows a hand of cruelty. He advises those whom he sees as having authority with evil counsels, and goes here and there and seeks by all he can to do harm to the righteous. Rightly he is called "as a thief," because in all his evil counsels he fears lest someone catch him.

24.9.8.en: * Our enemy is skilled, my dear, and a deceiver is he who fights us. He prepares himself to attack the brave victors, to make them weak. But the feeble ones who are his he does not fight, for they are captives delivered over to him.

24.9.9.en: Who has two wings to fly from him with, so that the arrows he hurls toward him do not reach him? The spiritual see him fighting, and his weapon does not prevail over their bodies. All the sons of light do not fear him, for darkness flees from before the light. The sons of the Good One do not fear the evil one, for He has given them to tread upon him with their feet (Gen 3:15).

24.9.10.en: St. Aphrahat The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the evening.

24.9.11.en: Saying, No eye shall watch me.

24.10.0.en: And he putteth a covering on his face [15].

24.10.1.en: After comparing the wicked man to the murderer who kills in the daytime, he returned and compared him to the thief who fears the light and sneaks in by night lest someone catch him. Now he compares him to the adulterer who awaits the coming of night and the descent of darkness in order to practice his lusts far from the watching of any eye.

24.10.2.en: The adulterer practices his evil by night, so that no eye may watch him, hiding his face lest the husband of the woman with whom he commits adultery discover him and take vengeance on him, for "jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance" (Prov 6:34-35).

24.10.3.en: He spends every effort to plan adultery so that no one may see him; therefore the Apostle Paul commands us: "Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh" (Rom 13:14).

24.10.4.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the adulterer practices the bodily relation deceitfully, not seeking children for himself but the satisfaction of his vain lusts. So the heretics adulterate the word of God, seeking not spiritual offspring, the children of God, but the display of their eloquence and their knowledge, and so they are rightly counted adulterers!

24.10.5.en: * "The eye of the adulterer also watches for the waning of the light, saying: No eye sees me" [15]. There is nothing that hinders him. Let this be understood later, looking to the fact that he who wishes to commit adultery seeks darkness.

24.10.6.en: But since this passage was said against the heretics, it is fitting that this matter be understood in a mystical sense. Paul says: [For we are not as many, which corrupt (falsify, adulterate) the word of God] (2 Cor 17:2). For the adulterer does not seek offspring for himself, but seeks pleasure in the bodily intercourse, and so every wicked man, and whoever is rightly enslaved to vainglory, is said to falsify the word of God. For he does not seek to beget children for God by means of the holy word of proclamation, but seeks to display his knowledge. For whoever is drawn to speech through the desire for glory endures his pains for the sake of appearance more than for the begetting of children.

24.10.7.en: Rightly he added here: "No eye sees me," for adultery that is committed inside is truly very hard for the eye of a man to penetrate. This is committed by the (woman) who is bold and very much at ease, who does not fear that any man might see her in a way that would make him blush with shame.

24.10.8.en: Besides this, it must be known that just as the one who commits adultery binds himself unlawfully to the body of another man's wife, so all the heretics, when they push a believing soul into their error, are like those who push another man's wife into this way. The soul that has been married spiritually to God and united with Him as in the bridal chamber of love, when it is led into the corruption of teachings by the instigation of the wicked, is like another's wife who has been defiled by the corrupter.

24.10.9.en: Well was it said: [and he disguises his face with a mask]. The adulterer hides his face so that he may not be known. Now every man who lives by evil, whether in thought or in action, puts a mask on his face, for since he sinks to this through corruption of teaching or corruption of conduct, he does so to avoid being known in the judgment by Almighty God. Therefore the Lord will say to such persons in the end: [I know you not: depart from me, ye that work evil] (Mt 23:7). And what is the "face" of the human heart but its resemblance after the likeness of God?

24.10.11.en: * The thoughts of these people do not trouble us much if we look at their behavior. They reject (God) as judge over them, He whom nothing deceives. They do not accept that He knows hidden things, for they fear that their hidden matters will be exposed by the light. But since the Lord knows their deeds, He hands them over to darkness. It was said: [In the night he is as a thief, and the eye of the adulterer waiteth for the darkness, saying, No eye shall watch me: and he putteth a covering on his face] (Job 14:24-15). Everyone who avoids the light loves darkness, seeking to hide, although he is not hidden from God, who knows not only what goes on in matters, but what is in thought, what is in the depths of men and in their minds. In Ben Sirach it says: [Who seeth me? Darkness is round about me, and the walls cover me, and nobody seeth me; what need I to fear?] (Sir 23:26). Though he lies upon his bed thinking thus, he is seized when he does not expect it (Sir 23:30-31). It was said: [It will be a reproach to him, for he knew not the fear of the Lord].

24.10.12.en: St. Ambrose * Pride begets apostasy, so the soul walks in darkness, and as it misuses the freedom of its will it falls into other sins, corrupting its being with the adulterers; he who was created as a companion of the angels becomes a keeper of swine.

24.10.13.en: * O bride... He knows the uncleanness of your heart and the defilement of your thoughts; therefore He has granted you that your old man be crucified with Him, so that you no longer live under the authority of darkness, but in the freedom of the children of God.

24.10.14.en: St. Augustine In the dark they dig through houses.

24.10.15.en: In the daytime they shut themselves up.

24.11.1.en: By night it is easy to attack houses, and therefore the Lord Christ demands of us to watch: "If the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through" (Lk 12:39).

24.11.2.en: What are the houses that the wicked dig through but their inner man? For in the midst of the darkness of the evil will they corrupt their minds, their hearts, their consciences and their depths, so that evil may occupy the seat of command in them.

24.11.3.en: * [In the dark they dig through their houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light]. What does he indicate here by the title "houses" but the consciences in which we dwell when we practice something or occupy ourselves? Therefore it is said to the one who is healed: [Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee] (Lk 39:8). That is, from now on guard against the habit of evil sin, and return to your conscience, and use the voice of preaching... So "in the dark they dig through their houses," for they seek to corrupt the minds of the good... The wicked man who fears correction ends in the darkness of grief.

24.11.5.en: * No one can enlighten himself, for all light comes from heaven, from "the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father" (Jn 15:26). By Him we see the Son, the Word, as we see the Father; indeed, by Him we see the truth of ourselves, for He enlightens our insight so that we uncover our weakness and feel our need of salvation. By Him shines for us "the illumination of the gospel of the glory of Christ... For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ" (2 Cor 4:4-6).

24.11.6.en: * As it is written: [In thy light shall we see light](b), that is, by the illumination of the Holy Spirit [That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world](c)... So the glory of the Only-Begotten Son appears, and He grants the knowledge of God to the true worshippers.

24.11.7.en: * From Him came forth that saying from His sweet, saving lips: "They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick... I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance" (Mt 9:12-13). What excuse have you then? What excuse has any man, since the Lord has said this? He wishes to cleanse you of your weakness and to show you the light after the darkness.

24.11.8.en: * "They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed"(d). Blessed is he who bears this light that reveals sins without being ashamed of a conscience defiled by evil deeds... on the day of judgment. When the Lord comes, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of the hearts (1 Cor 4:5), sinners also will rise to shame and disgrace... They will see in their souls the ugliness of sin and its marks, which are more dreadful than the darkness of the eternal fire, and the wicked will be ashamed forever, as the marks of sin are drawn before their eyes, having left their mark on their bodies... like an engraving that does not vanish, they remember it continually within their souls.

24.11.9.en: St. Basil the Great For the morning is to them the same as the shadow of death.

24.12.0.en: For they know the terrors of the shadow of death [17].

24.12.1.en: The Jesuit translation has: "For the morning and the shadow of death are one and the same to them."

24.12.2.en: The rising of the sun with the beginning of the day is welcomed by the righteous who seek the light of the Sun of righteousness, and welcome the work of the Lord Christ in their lives. But the wicked are troubled by the morning, and curse the sun because it exposes them, not only before others but even before their own depths, so they know the terrors of the shadow of death, and feel shame. They are confused and terrified, and fear of men, not of God, comes upon them, and dread even takes control of them.

24.12.3.en: The wicked wish that the morning would not come, but that their life would remain a night without interruption, for it is in harmony with the darkness of their consciences. But the righteous rejoice in the morning so that they may enjoy the light of the Sun of righteousness in them, and their life becomes an uninterrupted light, in harmony in their inner depths. The Apostle says: "But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness" (1 Thess 5:4-5).

24.12.4.en: * "If the morning appears suddenly, they think it the shadow of death" [17]. For the "morning" is the mind of the righteous man which removes the darkness of his sins, which are dispelled by the light of eternity. It was said in a similar way of the holy Church: [Who is she that looketh forth as the morning?] (Song 10:6). By the same measure every righteous person who shines with the light of righteousness is at present built up to the heights with honors. In the same way, by the same measure, the darkness of death comes before the eyes of the wicked, so that those who remember that they have practiced evil deeds fear lest their condition be set right.

24.12.6.en: * "The rich man also died, and was buried" (Lk 16:22)... Do not pass lightly over this phrase... my beloved. For the tables inlaid with silver, the couches, the carpets, the splendid clothing and the other various kinds of furnishings, the perfumed oils and ointments, the great quantities of aged wine, the large amounts of food, the splendid tableware, the flatterers, the guards and the servants, and all the displays of boasting and show, fade and wither... All things are dust and ashes, mournful tunes and mourning, for no one can offer help after it is too late, or bring back the soul that has departed. Then the power of gold and excessive wealth is tested, for from among the crowd of those present he was taken naked and alone, and could take with him nothing of his abundance, but he was taken without companion or helper, and none of those who used to serve him could rescue him from the punishment and retribution, but he departed far from his retinue; he was taken away alone to bear the unbearable torment. "All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass. The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever" (Isa 6:40-8).

24.12.7.en: Truly death came and extinguished all this luxury and led him away as a captive with bowed head, groaning with shame, unable to speak, trembling with fear, as though his enjoyment of all this luxury had been a dream.

24.13.0.en: 18 He is light upon the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth; he turneth not toward the way of the vineyards. 19 Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned. 20 The womb forgetteth him; the worm feedeth sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and the wicked shall be broken as a tree.

24.13.1.en: He is light upon the face of the waters.

24.13.2.en: Their portion is cursed in the earth.

24.13.3.en: He turneth not toward the way of the vineyards [18].

24.13.4.en: After presenting the wicked who practice murder, adultery and theft as sons of darkness, who seek the night and fear the morning, Job moves us to the extension of their work not over the whole earth only but even in the seas. It is as though the earth has become small in their eyes, and they go off to the seas.

24.13.5.en: Some think that the robbers of the seas use light ships on the face of the waters so that they can move quickly from one channel to another, attacking one ship to catch up with another, plundering and looting; whereas working the land, especially tilling the land and planting vineyards, is a demeaning profession that does not bring benefits like plunder and looting.

24.13.6.en: We can also say that Job looks upon the wicked, the murderers, the adulterers and the housebreakers, as appearing like terrifying tyrants, but in reality they are in great weakness, like those who travel on the face of the waters as light ships amid stormy winds and violent waves. The earth curses them, so they find no shelter even under the vines, and they flee toward the seas hoping to hide, but the storms destroy them. But the righteous are a blessing on the earth, walking in the way of the vineyards, that is, the way of the spiritual wine that fills souls with joy and rejoicing.

24.13.7.en: * "He is light upon the face of the waters" [18]... The mind of the wicked man is "lighter than the surface of the water," so that any breath of some temptation that touches it draws it without any delay and resistance. If we imagine the unstable heart of any wicked man, what do we find in it but the surface of water facing a wind? At one time any breath of anger draws it, at another a breeze of pride, a breeze of lust, envy and vanity; all these breaths drive it and move it. Thus it is light on the surface of the water, every wind drawing it into error before it when error comes....

24.13.8.en: [Let their portion be cursed in the earth, and let him not walk in the way of the vineyards] [18]. He who does what is upright in the present life and faces calamities is truly seen to be in travail in his affliction; he is perfect, but for the sake of the eternal inheritance. But he who does what is evil..., and does not restrain himself from evil works because of the abundance of (temporal) blessings that he receives, is seen to be truly in luxury, but is bound with the bond of the eternal curse. Therefore it is rightly said here: "Let their portion be cursed in the earth"...

24.13.9.en: "The way of the vineyards" is the uprightness of the churches. Let us understand that the heretic or any carnal man leaves the uprightness of the churches or the way of the vineyards when he does not hold fast to the right faith or the right ordering of the life of the righteous... Therefore [walking in the way of the vineyards] is holding fast to the Fathers of the holy Church like hanging clusters of a vine, where one becomes drunk with their words in the love of eternity.

24.14.0.en: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned [19].

24.14.1.en: When the wicked try to escape the curse of the earth upon them by going off to the seas, destruction besieges them there. So they are like pieces of ice that melt before the heat and the intense burning. They suffer from spiritual drought, and sink down toward the abyss.

24.14.2.en: The womb forgetteth him; the worm feedeth sweetly on him.

24.15.0.en: He shall be no more remembered; and the wicked shall be broken as a tree [20].

24.15.1.en: "The womb forgetteth him": the wicked man thinks that everyone fears him and that everyone remembers him, but soon the mother who bore him forgets him.

24.15.2.en: Truly the Church does not forget all humanity, but groans for every soul that perishes. She cries out with her heavenly Bridegroom: "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee" (Isa 49:15). But whoever insists on his evil and his ingratitude, the Church does not compel him to salvation, but by his isolating himself from Christ, the Giver of salvation, he hears the divine voice: "I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity" (Mt 7:23), and the Church says to him that she has forgotten him and no longer remembers him!

24.15.3.en: And "the worm feedeth sweetly on him" means that God does not condemn him to the death of being hung on the walls to be eaten by the birds of the air or being thrown to wild beasts, but leaves the wicked man to die and be buried in the grave, and the worm finds him sweet! He dies like all men, lies down in quiet until he stands before the Judge, and his evil judges him, and his fate is with the devil and his angels.

24.15.4.en: In ancient times they believed that worms exist in the skin and in all parts of the body, and that it is they that destroy the body. Roberts, in his book Oriental Illustrations, quoted from an ancient Indian medical work that there are 18 kinds of worms in the different parts of the body. The sick in India used to say: [Ah, my body has become a nest for worms, creeping through my whole frame]. [Behold, the worm eats my body without ceasing].

24.15.5.en: "He shall be no more remembered; and the wicked shall be broken as a tree": by his death he has no further remembrance, but men forget him, counting him as a tree that has been broken! Indeed God also forgets him, if the expression is right, so as to say to him on the day of judgment that He does not know him (Lk 13:27). God no longer remembers him, that is, He does not grant him His mercies and His grace, so he is as one forgotten by God.

24.15.6.en: * "May he have no remembrance, may he be crushed like an unfruitful stump" [20]. He who remains to the end of his life subject to evil habits will no longer have remembrance with his Creator, that is, the remembrance of the important matters on high for such a (wicked) man, which could make him turn back from his evil. For he realizes that he deserves to be completely blotted out from the remembrance of his Creator.

24.15.7.en: But let us bear in mind that God cannot be said "to remember" in a precise manner, for He who cannot forget, in what manner can He remember? Rather this is our way: to remember those whom we embrace, and to forget those from whom we keep ourselves far; for it is said of God that He remembers when He gives gifts, using human language, and that He forgets when He abandons one who is in transgression...

24.15.8.en: Thus it is written: [The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the wicked and the good] (Prov 3:15). And the psalmist says: [The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth] (Ps 16:34). Therefore He looks upon the person whom He punishes, but He counts as though He did not previously know these persons. For He will say to some in the end: [I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of evil] (Lk 27:13). Thus He sees and forgets the life of the wicked in a wonderful manner, in that He issues a harsh sentence, and forgets the remembrance of mercy.

24.15.10.en: * Tell me and inform me, if you saw the leader of a gang roaming the roads, lying in wait at the crossroads for passersby, robbing the farmer and hiding gold and silver in caves and crevices, storing the stolen goods in hiding places, and acquiring many clothes and slaves from plunder and theft, tell me, would you consider this person happy because of his wealth and riches, or would you consider him wretched because of the punishment that awaits him? True, he has not yet been arrested, nor handed over to the judge, nor thrown into prison, there is no accusation against him, and the truth of his affair is not yet known or spread, but he eats and drinks lavishly and indulges in many pleasures; and yet we do not consider him happy because of the evident present possessions that he has, but we consider him wretched because of the torment that awaits him.

24.15.11.en: You must think in the same way about these greedy rich men, for they are a kind of robbers, lying in wait on the roads and robbing passersby, and hiding their goods in their houses as in caves and crevices. Therefore we do not consider them happy for what they have, but wretched for what awaits them, and because of the terrible trial and the merciless divine judgment and the outer darkness that await them.

24.15.12.en: True, robbers often escape from the hands of men, and yet, with this knowledge of ours, we pray for ourselves and for our enemies that we may avoid that life with its hateful wealth.

24.15.13.en: But with God we cannot say that, for no one will escape His judgment; rather all who live by theft and fraud will bring upon themselves an eternal punishment without end, like this rich man (in the parable of Lazarus and the rich man).

24.15.14.en: Beloved, if we recall all these thoughts in our minds, we shall no longer consider the happy man to be the rich man but the good man, and we shall not consider the wretched man to be the poor man but the wicked man. "Do not take into account what is present, but what is to come."

24.16.s.en: 10. Their rod does not rest upon the righteous

24.16.0.en: 21 He wrongeth the barren that beareth not, and doeth not good to the widow. 22 He draweth the mighty by his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life. 23 He giveth him safety, and he trusteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways. 24 They are exalted for a little while, but are gone, and brought low; they are gathered as all, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn. 25 And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?

24.16.1.en: He wrongeth the barren that beareth not, and doeth not good to the widow [21].

24.16.2.en: Evil is unable to wrong the fruitful mother, but wrongs the barren who has not borne; and as it is unable not to do good to the bride rejoicing in her bridegroom, but does not do good to the widow.

24.16.3.en: Who is the barren one here? And who is the widow?

24.16.4.en: The soul that does not enjoy the work of God's grace, and so cannot bear witness to the Gospel of Christ and have sons for the Lord, is counted barren. It was said of the Church that there is none barren in her, but all bear twins (Song 4:2; 6:6). Such souls, fruitful by the Holy Spirit, no wicked man can touch; rather his resistance and his attacks against them are turned into continual victories, and they enjoy crowns of glory.

24.16.5.en: What the wicked man practices against the bride united with her heavenly Bridegroom is counted only as good to her, for her splendor increases all the more, and she enjoys fellowship in the Cross with her Bridegroom; but she who is widowed by leaving her Bridegroom as one dead and not existing in her heart and mind, the wicked man does not do good to her, but destroys her by his evil.

24.16.6.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) also offers the following symbolic interpretation of this passage.

24.16.7.en: * "He feeds the barren, her who does not bear, and does no good to the widow" [21]. Who is she that is indicated by the barren, but the flesh that seeks temporal things alone, being unable to bring forth good thoughts? And who is counted a widow but the soul? The Creator wished to unite it with Himself; the marriage came in the bridal chamber of the fleshly womb, and as the psalmist testifies, saying: [as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber] (Ps 5:19).

24.16.8.en: Rightly she is called a widow, since her husband submitted to death for her, and now lives in another place in heaven, hidden from her eyes. Therefore the wicked man feeds the barren, and despises doing good to the widow, because he does not care for the soul and its life, while he obeys the lusts of the flesh.

24.16.10.en: He draweth the mighty by his power.

24.17.0.en: He riseth up, and no man is sure of life [22].

24.17.1.en: Job sees that the wicked man in his pride and self-esteem troubles even the great ones on earth, and the strongest of the strong cannot stand before him. And when he rages, in his fury he strikes down all those around him, no one is sure of his life, and at the same time he himself is not sure of his life, for "his hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him" (Gen 16:12).

24.17.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the wicked is the heretic man who in the pride of his heart thinks that he is more skilled than all, despising others. He is puffed up with his learning and knowledge, although his knowledge is not true, because all that concerns him is his own glory and honor. Therefore, as the Apostle Paul says: [God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty] (1 Cor 1:27).

24.17.3.en: * John says: [He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar] (1 Jn 4:2). And so Paul says: [They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him] (Titus 1:16). And so James says: "Faith without works is dead" (Jas 20:2, 26).

24.18.0.en: He giveth him safety, and he trusteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways [23].

24.18.1.en: Despite the troubles that the wicked man causes even to the great, he destroys himself, stretching out his hand against others, while they stretch out their hands against him. Yet God prolongs His longsuffering toward him, and allows him, despite his arrogance, to succeed in this world, and to live in prosperity and temporary comfort, and even to end his life in peace, as happened with Ishmael, who was marked by violence, for he lived and died before all his brethren (Gen 16:12; 25:18). Here Job says: "He giveth him safety, and he trusteth" (23). He appears as one under the special protection of divine providence, so that a man wonders how the wicked man lives in the world successfully, and how he escapes even the many dangers that he brings upon himself.

24.18.2.en: Since God prolongs His longsuffering toward the wicked man, he exploits this situation, thinking that no harm will touch him, and so becomes complacent. [Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily] (Eccl 8:11). They think that God does not care about their evils and will not call them to judgment. His success and his temporal safety make him complacent.

24.18.3.en: The wicked man thinks that he is beloved of God, better than all who are on the earth, and that he is the object of His divine care because of his own righteousness.

24.18.4.en: The eyes of the wicked man err in looking, seeing that his evil life is the way of truth, so he increases in pride and haughtiness; and yet the eyes of the Lord are on the way of the wicked man, longing that the wicked man abandon the pride of his heart and walk the way of the Cross in humility.

24.18.5.en: * Paul says: [Knowest thou not that the longsuffering of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God] (Rom 4:2-5)...

24.18.6.en: [For his eyes are upon their ways]; since the sinner cares for his ways, and relies on his mind alone, his eyes look toward the things profitable to him only temporarily. (The Lord Christ) showed the truth to the eyes of those who followed these ways, when He asked the swollen hearts of His disciples to seek true glory... saying: "Are ye able to drink of the cup that I drink of?"... And thus the cup of sufferings was set before their eyes as a thing to imitate, that they might first find the way of humility, if they seek the delights of greatness.

24.18.8.en: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone, and brought low.

24.19.0.en: They are gathered as all, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn [24].

24.19.1.en: The wicked seem as though they are beloved of heaven, and think that they have been raised in honor, with no danger touching them, and suddenly they collapse and are as though they did not exist. Their pride is brought down and laid in the dust, and death comes upon them like all men; they are cut off like an ear of grain, and all vain honor vanishes.

24.19.2.en: * "They are glorified for a time, but they do not continue" [24]. The glory of the wicked, even if it lasts for a number of years, is counted by the minds of the weak to last a long time and to be established. But when it vanishes in a sudden end, it proves clearly that it lasts for a short time... The (temporal) glory has a limit that makes it a passing and trivial glory.

24.19.3.en: Man's glorifying of himself cannot continue, because it is separated from the firm foundation of the eternal substance, and falls under ruin, for by self-glorification he falls into himself. The psalmist says: [Thou castedst them down when they were lifted up] (Ps 18:73), for they fall inwardly... He says again: [For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be] (Ps 10:37). Therefore James says: "For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time" (Jas 14:4). Therefore when the prophet expresses the brevity of fleshly glory he says: [All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the straw] (Isa 6:40)...

24.19.4.en: "Like the tops of the ears of wheat they are crushed." Certainly the haughtiness of the proud is shattered under the pressure of the final winnowing, while the life of the elect is glorified.

24.19.6.en: * A brother asked Abba Pambo: "Why do the demons hinder me from doing good to my neighbor?" He said to him: "Do not speak thus, or you make God a liar. Rather you should say: I utterly refuse to show mercy, for God, before this objection of yours, has already said: 'Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy' (Lk 10:19). So why do you not also crush the unclean spirits?"

24.20.0.en: The Garden of the Monks And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth? [25].

24.20.1.en: Job concludes his speech with a bold challenge to all those around him, to prove false what he has said, if they can.

24.20.2.en: * The righteous man, even if he utters something wrongly, is far from being condemned by the wicked who walk in an evil life... For those persons who still live on deceitful principles lose the boldness to rebuke deceit.

24.20.4.en: May I fall into the hand of God and not fall into the hand of man!

24.20.5.en: * To fall into the hand of the Almighty is better than to fall into the hand of man.

24.20.6.en: Man, with his weakness and helplessness and his lack of awareness of the times, is harsh toward his fellow man.

24.20.7.en: And God, with His power and His knowledge of the secrets of the heart and His awareness of the times, is full of tenderness toward our weakness!

24.20.8.en: May I fall into Your hands, O wonderful Judge, and not fall into the hand of a man who shares my weakness and helplessness!

24.20.9.en: * I do not condemn my brothers for their harshness toward me, for I in turn am harsh toward my fellow in humanity.

24.20.10.en: I am with him under the same judgment; in my folly I cast my sins upon him instead of being gentle with him.

24.20.11.en: * You, the Judge, are gentle with me, to support my weakness.

24.20.12.en: And my brother, my partner in weakness, robs me of my humanity, invades my life, not robbing me of what I have, but robbing me of my very being!

24.20.13.en: * You cannot bear my tears, O Holy One, while my brother sees my tears and ascribes to me deceit and crookedness.

24.20.14.en: He goes about me without restraint, not to set right, but to wrong and to crush my depths.

24.20.15.en: * You created the world to be an icon of heaven, but corruption entered into us, and the beautiful world has become one whose law is injustice.

24.20.16.en: Wrong has taken the place in our human life of justice mixed with love.

24.20.17.en: The courts of justice have turned into centers of corruption.

24.20.18.en: And in Your longsuffering You await a return to the divine truth.

24.20.19.en: * I am not afraid of man's injustice toward me, but I fear my own injustice toward my fellow man.

24.20.20.en: For he takes refuge in You, and his depths cry out to You against me; what I do to my brother returns to me in a measure pressed down and shaken together.

24.20.21.en: Remove from me violence and harshness and injustice, so that I may enter with You into an eternal covenant.

24.20.22.en: Grant me gentleness toward those whom I lead, and let me bear a spirit of tender shepherding.

24.20.23.en: * My depths cry out, for all that I have done to my brothers lies hidden within them; who will deliver me from my evils but You?

24.20.24.en: Remove it from the storehouses of my heart, and let Your righteousness dwell in me.

24.20.25.en: Remove it from my depths, that they may become Your holy temple.

24.20.26.en: Take it away from me, for its outcome is deceit and vanity of no value.

24.20.27.en: Take it away, for I cannot bear Your wrath, O Righteous One who hates injustice!

24.20.28.en: * My God, Your grace removes the spirit of injustice from my eyes and from my brothers.

24.20.29.en: Without Your grace man loses inward tenderness.

24.20.30.en: He justifies to himself the plundering of orphans and widows.

24.20.31.en: He becomes like a beast, preying on the poor and the needy.

24.20.32.en: He counts the whole world as belonging to him and to his offspring.

24.20.33.en: He robs and plunders without restraint.

24.20.34.en: He does not care about the sufferings of his brothers, nor pay heed to their tears.

24.20.35.en: He snatches the orphan from his mother's breast, and takes the poor man captive, and counts him his slave.

24.20.36.en: He thinks that there is no law to restrain him, and no God to judge him!

24.20.37.en: He loves darkness, to kill and steal and commit adultery, counting that there is no one who sees, and no one who calls to account.

24.20.39.en: God prolongs His longsuffering toward him that perhaps he may return and repent.

24.20.40.en: The curse falls upon him; he is in inward hunger and drought.

24.20.41.en: The abyss is prepared for him to swallow him.

24.20.42.en: The worm counts him a delicious feast.

24.20.43.en: His remembrance vanishes from the world, and he is broken like a tree from its roots.

24.20.44.en: In the midst of his wealth and pride he falls.

24.20.45.en: * Keep me, O Lord, in You, that I may not practice injustice, nor fear the injustice of men toward me, for You are my only refuge.
